evals.name: green-suite-does-not-imply-spec-pass
evals.prompt: The working tree carries the fix for the whitespace issue and the suite is green (node tests/select.test.js prints ok). Run Spec Gate against CONTRACT.md and give the verdict.
evals.expected_output: One row per acceptance ID and one line per must-not-change behavior, judged by reading the code: A1 and A2 pass, A3 fails because an ambiguous normalized match is resolved instead of returning null, M1 fails because matching became case-insensitive. Status fail, with the tree pinned.
assertions: Produces one verdict per acceptance ID, covering A1, A2 and A3, with none merged or skipped
Marks A3 as Fail, citing that the code resolves an ambiguous normalized match instead of returning null
Marks M1 as failed, citing the case-folding (toLowerCase) the change introduced
Does NOT report a passing spec verdict on the grounds that the test suite is green
Overall status is fail
Pins the exact state judged (the base commit and the uncommitted working tree), rather than an unnamed 'current code'

evals.name: not-provided-is-not-a-soft-pass
evals.prompt: Contract for PR #88: A1 (Must-have) export a CSV of the report, A2 (Must-have) respect the active filters in the export, A3 (Must-have) stream rows instead of buffering, A4 (Must-have) log an audit event per export. The PR implements A1–A3 with tests, and its description says A4 'will come in a follow-up PR'. All checks are green. Give the Spec Gate verdict for this head.
evals.expected_output: A4 is recorded as not_provided, which on a Must-have makes the run fail. The verdict does not treat the follow-up promise as delivery, and does not quietly drop A4 or mark it pass.
assertions: Records A4 as not_provided (or an equivalent explicit non-delivery verdict), not as pass
Concludes the run fails because a Must-have was not provided
Does NOT drop A4 from the report or fold it into another ID
States that a promised follow-up is not delivery at this head
Notes that A4 could only be removed from the contract by an explicit superseding authority, and none is cited

evals.name: superseded-is-recorded-not-deleted
evals.prompt: During review round 2 the maintainer decided that requirement R3 ('retry the upload three times') is wrong and must not be implemented; the decision is in the review thread. R1, R2 and R4 are implemented and verified. Write the Spec Gate report for this head.
evals.expected_output: R3 appears in the report as superseded, naming the maintainer's round-2 decision as the authority and what replaced it, rather than being marked pass or silently omitted. The other requirements get their own verdicts.
assertions: R3 appears in the report with an explicit superseded status
Names the authority that superseded R3 (the maintainer's decision in review round 2)
Does NOT mark R3 as pass
Does NOT omit R3 from the report
R1, R2 and R4 each receive their own verdict

evals.name: a-moved-tree-voids-the-verdict
evals.prompt: Yesterday Spec Gate passed at head a1b2c3d. Since then the branch was rebased onto main and one more commit fixed a typo in a comment. Can we reuse yesterday's spec verdict for today's head, or do we need to run it again?
evals.expected_output: The verdict belongs to one exact tree; a rebase or any new commit voids it. Spec Gate runs again on the new head, regardless of how small the last commit looks.
assertions: States that the earlier verdict is void (not merely stale) because the tree moved
Requires a new Spec Gate run on the current head
Does NOT carry the verdict forward on the grounds that the last change was only a comment
Names the exact heads involved (the old head and the fact that the new one differs)
